texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this writ petition Patna High Court CWJC No.15039 of 2025(2) dt.15-09-2025 challenging the Memorandum No. 155 dated 19.10.2024, 176 dated 11.12.2024 & 184 Dr Sudhir Kumar Jain vs The Union Of India on 15 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163464781/ 1 dated 27.12.2024 issued by the Chief Vigilance Officer by which departmental proceeding have been initiated against the petitioner under Rule 14 & 16 of the Central Civil Services (Classification Control and Appeal) rules 1965.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that departmental proceeding initiated against the petitioner pertains to the incident that has taken place in the year 2016- 2021. 4. Praying for an interim order of stay of the departmental proceeding, learned senior counsel has contended that a departmental proceeding against the petitioner cannot be initiated for the incidents that have taken place eight years and three years back in the year 2016 and 2021 respectively. For the proposition that the departmental proceeding cannot be initiated at a belated stage, learned senior counsel has relied on a decision rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of M.P. v. Bani Singh, reported in AIR 1990 SC 1308. 5. Secondly, it has been contended that the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in a somewhat similar state of facts in the CWJC NO. 11558 of 2025 vide order dated 24.07.2025 has stayed the departmental proceeding initiated against the Patna High Court CWJC No.15039 of 2025(2) dt.15-09-2025 petitioner. 6. Thirdly, it has been contended that the disciplinary authority of the petitioner who is a Professor of the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, hereinafter referred to as "University" is the "Board of Management" as defined in Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University Act, 2016 (for short the "Act"). As per the resolution of the "Board of Management", it is the Vice Chancellor who has been authorized for approving appointment of Inquiry Officer and presenting Officers, issuance of charge-sheets, taking day to day decisions relating to the inquiry proceedings under the CCA(CCS) rules, 1965 and submitting the inquiry report to the Board of Management for taking decisions in the case, wherein the "Board of Management" is the disciplinary authority. He then contends that the Vice Chancellor who himself is a delegatee of the Board has further delegated the power of issuance of charge-sheet to the Chief Vigilance Officer which is not permissible. 6.1. In support of his contention that the Vice Chancellor could not have further delegated the power of issuance of charge-sheet to the Chief Vigilance Officer, learned senior counsel has relied on a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Patna High Court CWJC No.15039 of 2025(2) dt.15-09-2025 Court in the case of A.K. Roy v. State of Punjab, reported in AIR 1986 SC 2160. 7. 8. With regard to the first contention advanced by the learned senior counsel for the petitioner by referring to the case of Bani Singh (supra); that was a case wherein the Administrative Tribunal had [LEAKAGE_MASK] the departmental proceeding initiated against the petitioner therein, after a lapse of 12 years. On an appeal preferred by the State of Madhya Pradesh, the Hon'ble Supreme Court did not interfere with the order of the Tribunal quashing the departmental proceeding initiated against the petitioner therein, after a lapse of 12 years but it appears that Hon'ble Supreme Court in that case did not lay down a proposition of law having universal application, whereby any time limit has been Dr Sudhir Kumar Jain vs The Union Of India on 15 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163464781/ 2 fixed for initiation of a departmental proceeding against the employee. 9. The second contention of the petitioner is by referring to an order passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in CWJC No. 11558 of 2025 in which writ petition the departmental proceeding initiated against the petitioner therein with regard to the age and experience of the petitioner therein at Patna High Court CWJC No.15039 of 2025(2) dt.15-09-2025 the time of his appointment as Associate Professor in the University was put to challenge. 10. With regard to the third contention regarding delegation by the Vice Chancellor of the University to the Chief Vigilance Officer for serving of a memorandum of charges to the petitioner, I have perused the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of A.K. Roy (supra) relied on by the learned senior counsel for the petitioner and on perusal thereof I find that, that was a case arising in the context of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 wherein notification issued by the Food (Health) Authority in so far as it purported to delegate the powers to institute prosecutions for an offence under Section Patna High Court CWJC No.15039 of 2025(2) dt.15-09-2025 20(1) of the Act to the Food Inspector was held to be ultra vires. 11. At this stage learned senior counsel makes a fourth submission by contending that the memorandum of charge has not been approved by the Board of Management of the University as is Dr Sudhir Kumar Jain vs The Union Of India on 15 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163464781/ 3 required in terms of the provision contained in the Act itself. In support of this contention learned senior counsel has relied on a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India v. B.V. Gopinath, reported in (2014) 1 SCC 351. 12.
